body:
Refers to the structures, policies, practices, and culture that protect people from harm while enabling sport to be delivered effectively. It covers the full operating environment of the organisation, including facilities, programmes, events, staff, volunteers, athletes, participants, spectators, contractors, and community stakeholders.

A sport organisation has a duty to ensure that safety is planned, managed, communicated, and continuously improved. This means identifying risks before activities take place, putting in place appropriate controls, preparing for emergencies, and learning from incidents when they occur.

Safety should be embedded into everyday decision-making rather than treated as a separate compliance exercise.

vision: A sport ecosystem where every participant, athlete, coach, and official can pursue sport safely and with confidence — free from injury, abuse, and preventable harm.
mission: To embed safety as a core value across all sport organisations, programmes, events, and facilities in Singapore through leadership, clear standards, practical guidance, and active partnership.

body: The overarching policy connecting the organisation's individual safety policies into one coherent framework.

content.heading: Purpose
content.text: The Integrated Safety Policy establishes the organisation's commitment to providing a safe environment for all individuals involved in sport delivery — including athletes, participants, coaches, officials, staff, volunteers, contractors, and spectators. It connects and aligns the Sport Safety Policy, Safe Sport Policy, and Workplace Safety and Health Policy into a single coherent framework, ensuring that safety obligations are understood, communicated, and upheld consistently across all programmes, events, facilities, and partnerships.

content.heading: Scope
content.text: This policy applies to all activities conducted or supported by the organisation, including sport programmes, training sessions, competitions, community events, facility operations, and administrative functions.

content.heading: Commitments
content.text: The organisation commits to maintaining a culture where safety is a shared value, not merely a compliance requirement; allocating adequate resources to safety planning, training, and incident management; setting measurable safety objectives and monitoring progress against them; ensuring that safety considerations are embedded in all decision-making processes; and reviewing and improving safety performance on a continuous basis.

content.heading: Roles and Responsibilities
content.text: Leadership is responsible for setting direction and ensuring accountability. All staff, coaches, and partners are responsible for implementing safety requirements within their areas of operation and for reporting concerns promptly through the appropriate channels.

content.heading: Review
content.text: This policy will be reviewed annually or following a significant incident, regulatory change, or material shift in the organisation's operating environment.

body: Sets the baseline safety standards expected across all supported sport activity.

content.heading: Purpose
content.text: The Sport Safety Policy establishes the minimum safety standards required for the delivery of all sport activities under the organisation's remit. It applies to all programmes, training sessions, competitions, and events, whether delivered directly or through accredited partners. The purpose is to reduce the risk of physical injury, environmental harm, and equipment-related incidents across all sport delivery settings.

content.heading: Key Requirements
content.text: All individuals delivering sport activities are required to conduct a risk assessment prior to any activity or event; ensure that facilities and equipment meet applicable safety standards before use; hold current and relevant safety certifications appropriate to their role; brief participants on safety procedures before commencing activity; and have an emergency response plan in place, communicated to all relevant personnel.

content.heading: Incident Reporting
content.text: Any injury, near-miss, or unsafe condition must be reported through the organisation's incident reporting system as soon as practicable. All reports will be reviewed and investigated in accordance with the organisation's incident management procedure. Reporting is not optional — it is a core safety obligation for all staff, coaches, and partners.

content.heading: Compliance
content.text: Failure to comply with this policy may result in suspension of programme approval, revocation of accreditation, or other appropriate action. Partners and contractors are required to demonstrate compliance as a condition of their engagement with the organisation.

content.heading: Review
content.text: This policy is reviewed annually or following any significant safety incident or change in applicable standards.

body: Covers safeguarding, athlete welfare, and protection from abuse or harassment in sport.

content.heading: Purpose
content.text: The Safe Sport Policy reflects the organisation's commitment to ensuring that every individual — regardless of age, ability, gender, or background — can participate in sport in an environment that is safe, respectful, and free from all forms of harm. It establishes the standards and obligations required to protect athletes, participants, coaches, officials, and support personnel from abuse, harassment, discrimination, and exploitation.

content.heading: Prohibited Conduct
content.text: The following conduct is strictly prohibited in all sport settings: physical, emotional, or sexual abuse of any kind; bullying, intimidation, or coercive behaviour; discrimination based on race, gender, age, disability, religion, or sexual orientation; and grooming or inappropriate relationships between those in positions of authority and participants in their care. These prohibitions apply in all environments — on and off the field, in person, and online.

content.heading: Reporting and Response
content.text: Any individual who witnesses or experiences conduct prohibited under this policy is encouraged and supported to report it. Reports may be made to a designated Safe Sport officer or through the organisation's confidential reporting channel. All reports will be treated with sensitivity and confidentiality, and investigated promptly and impartially by appropriately trained personnel.

content.heading: Support for Affected Persons
content.text: The organisation will provide appropriate support to anyone affected by a Safe Sport concern, including referral to counselling, legal advice, or other services as required. The welfare of the affected person is the primary consideration at every stage of the reporting and investigation process.

content.heading: Review
content.text: This policy is reviewed annually and updated in response to legislative changes, sector guidance, or lessons learned from reported cases.

body: The organisation's Workplace Safety and Health obligations for staff, contractors, and facility operators.

content.heading: Purpose
content.text: The Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Policy establishes the organisation's commitment to providing a safe and healthy working environment for all staff, volunteers, contractors, and other workers involved in sport delivery and facility operations. It is aligned with applicable workplace safety and health legislation and with the ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System standard.

content.heading: Scope
content.text: This policy applies to all workplaces operated or managed by the organisation, including sport facilities, offices, event venues, and any other locations where work is carried out on behalf of the organisation. It extends to contractors and service providers engaged to work on the organisation's premises or programmes.

content.heading: Key Commitments
content.text: The organisation commits to: identifying and eliminating or controlling workplace hazards through systematic risk assessment; providing safe plant, equipment, and working systems; ensuring workers are competent to perform their tasks safely through appropriate training and supervision; consulting with workers on matters affecting their health and safety; and investigating all workplace incidents, near-misses, and dangerous occurrences promptly and thoroughly.

content.heading: Responsibilities
content.text: Management is responsible for resourcing and overseeing the implementation of this policy. All workers share responsibility for maintaining a safe workplace by following safe work procedures, using provided safety equipment, and reporting hazards and incidents without delay. No worker will be disadvantaged for raising a safety concern in good faith.

content.heading: Review
content.text: This policy is reviewed annually or following any workplace incident, regulatory change, or audit finding that warrants revision.

items.heading: Commitments
points: Provide a safe environment for all individuals involved in sport delivery.
Allocate adequate resources to safety planning, training, and incident management.
Ensure safety considerations are embedded in all decision-making processes.
Consult with workers and stakeholders on matters affecting their safety.
Maintain a culture where safety is a shared value, not merely a compliance requirement.

items.heading: Objectives
points: Achieve zero fatalities and reduce serious injuries across all sport programmes.
Ensure all sport organisations adopt and implement an Integrated Safety Management System.
Attain full compliance with applicable Singapore Standards and Codes of Practice.
Build safety leadership capability at Board and Chief Executive level.
Strengthen incident reporting culture and response timeliness.

items.heading: Targets
points: 100% of affiliated sport organisations to complete safety framework assessment by end of year.
All high-risk sport programmes to have documented emergency response plans.
Reduce incident recurrence rate through structured after-action reviews.
Annual safety audit completed for all sport centres under management.
Safety training completion rate of 90% or above for all frontline staff and coaches.

body: Safety decisions flow from the Board through the Safety Governance function to operational teams and facility-level Safety Officers, each with defined authority to act.
The organisation and its partners operate under applicable Workplace Safety and Health legislation and related regulations, alongside sport-specific statutory requirements.
Everyone delivering or hosting sport activity — staff, coaches, event operators, and partners — shares a duty of care to participants, spectators, and each other.
